reader.requirement: At --std 85 a reference modifier must be evaluated immediately after the operand's subscripts (applied per element for an ALL subscript), at the time subscripting would be evaluated for an unsubscripted operand (so under each statement's own timing: once at statement start by default, before the first receiver for a MOVE sender, before each receiver for a MOVE receiver, before the examination for UNSTRING receivers), and immediately after the function is evaluated in a function reference.
reader.edition-search: grep of Edition|CobolVersion|Dialect in RefModBinder.cs and PlaceRenderer.cs (diagnostic sinks only); the RefModPlace start/length are frozen with the operand's identification by the same emitter path at every --std. The only edition-dependent behaviour met was the §1985:VI.6.25.3 SR3 refusal of a reference-modified STRING INTO item, which is another rule.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf05_01 and pb5209 cover a (subscripted, ALL), b for a MOVE receiver, c (REVERSE); not exercised: a MOVE sender whose modifier's start is a receiver, UNSTRING INTO receivers whose modifier depends on an earlier receiver, STRING senders with the POINTER item as the start, a function argument itself reference-modified

probes.printed: M1 K=3 Y=3 | U1 K=4 Y=Q.... | S1 K=5 Z=.bcb. | T1 ABCD2FGHI | F1=[C] | F2=[cb]
probes.expected: MOVE X(K:1) TO K Y: sender evaluated once before the first receiver (Y=3); UNSTRING INTO K Y(K:1): evaluated once before examination, so Y(1:1)=Q; STRING X(K:2) X(K:1) ... POINTER K: evaluated at statement start (.bcb., K=5); MOVE 2 TO J TE(J)(J:1): subscript then modifier after J=2 (ABCD2FGHI); UPPER-CASE(X(2:3))(2:1)=C; REVERSE(X(2:3))(2:2)=cb

probes.printed: error COBOL1651: STRING INTO 'Z (K:4)': identifier-3 shall not be reference-modified
probes.expected: refused at 1985 by §1985:VI.6.25.3 SR3 (Identifier-3 must not be reference modified)

citations.check: OK  §1985:IV.4.3.8.4.4 GR3  (4.3.8.4.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR3

reader.notes: Every timing arm GR3 names, combined with the statement timings of §1985:IV.4.3.8 (evaluated once as the first operation), MOVE GR2 and the UNSTRING change, gave the expected result. The modifier is part of the frozen place identification, so it is evaluated with the subscripts and never re-read mid-statement.

refuter.evidence: Probe refute-1985-088/src/p2.cob at --std 85 (run p2-001), aimed at timings the reader did not try. MOVE '3' TO K Y(K:1) gave Y=..3.. (the receiver's modifier is evaluated before its own move, after K, §1985:VI.6.19.4 GR2). INSPECT X(K:3) TALLYING K FOR ALL 'A' gave K=3 (evaluated once at the start, not re-read as K grows). Format 3 INSPECT X(K:6) TALLYING K ... REPLACING ALL 'A' BY Y(K:1) gave X=ppbppc with K=5 (the BY operand is evaluated with K=1 before the tally, §1985:VI.6.18.4 GR17). UNSTRING ... INTO K Y DELIMITER IN D(K:1) COUNT IN CT gave D=,.... (the DELIMITER IN modifier is evaluated once, before examination, with K=1). FUNCTION MAX(TE(ALL)(2:1)) gave 9 (the modifier is applied to each ALL element). FUNCTION REVERSE(TE(K))(K:1) gave 1 (the modifier is applied after the function). Every result is what the text gives. cite.py: OK §1985:IV.4.3.8.4.4 GR3 the text is in GR3; OK §1985:VI.6.19.4 GR2 the text is in GR2; OK §1985:VI.6.18.4 GR17 the text is in GR17.
